question.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z}4xz\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{4-2y}\}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z}4xz\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}[2z{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=z}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2z({z}^{2}-0)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}2{z}^{3}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2{z}^{3}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-2y}}2{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=\sqrt{4-2y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{4-2y)})^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(4-2y)^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2}(16-16y+4{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}8-8y+2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[8y-4{y}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =16-16+\frac{16}{3} \\  & =\frac{16}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
